title: HUMANKIND II

story.logline: A newborn repeatedly opens its eyes at different moments in human history, moving from prehistory to the near future and reframing civilisation as a series of beginnings.
story.theme: history, civilisation and the possibility of beginning again
story.character_goal: The newborn has no conventional goal; the viewer's goal is to discover the changing world through its point of view.
story.obstacle: Each historical world is unfamiliar and unstable, while the point of view remains limited to a newborn's first perception.
story.turning_choice: The film uses one consistent point of view and repeats the birth event across eras rather than changing to an external narrator.
story.result: The repeated structure makes the game's central promise—building one's own history—memorable.

beats.visible_action: A newborn opens its eyes into a prehistoric world.
beats.state_out: viewer accepts newborn point of view
beats.evidence: campaign description states the camera takes the newborn's perspective

beats.visible_action: The same birth perspective opens onto different civilisations and historical crises.
beats.state_out: history becomes a pattern of beginnings
beats.evidence: description lists Neolithic, plague, frontier and wartime settings

beats.visible_action: The births progress toward a spacecraft and near-future setting.
beats.evidence: the final birth occurs aboard a spacecraft orbiting Earth

beats.visible_action: The repeated device resolves into the game's invitation to build history.
beats.evidence: campaign is a launch film for a strategy game about building history

scene_functions: establish a formal point of view
rules_observed: Repetition can create progression when each repetition changes scale, context or meaning.
anti_patterns: A repeated visual gimmick without contextual escalation becomes a montage without narrative accumulation.
quality_notes: Strong example of concept-led launch film; not directly transferable to a 30-second product demonstration.
